ca_shooting_gallery_center.blurb: Shooting Gallery Center is the middle cluster of the Shooting Gallery crags, part of the Lake Arrowhead Pinnacles in the San Bernardino Mountains. It has eight routes, split evenly between bolted lines and trad climbs on monzogranite. The grades start around 5.6 and top out in the 5.10 range, with a couple of routes at each of 5.6, 5.9 and 5.10 and singles at 5.7 and 5.8, so it suits a mixed party that wants both moderate climbs and a few harder ones. The routes are short. To get here, follow the trail up past Hone Pinnacle, which makes it a bit further in than the first walls you reach.

ca_super_fun_site.blurb: Super Fun Site is a broad, U-shaped hanging valley set above Scheelite Wall in Pine Creek Canyon, in the Bishop area of the Eastern Sierra. It holds eight routes on granodiorite, five of them trad and three bolted. Grades run from 5.9 up to 5.13, but most of the climbing sits in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, so it is a place for confident leaders rather than beginners. Reaching it is part of the outing: the way in involves roped fifth-class climbing on the wall below, followed by scree, rather than a plain trail walk.

ca_sister_boulder.blurb: Sister Boulder is a pair of boulders in the Family Boulders group near Lake George, above Mammoth Lakes in the Eastern Sierra, at roughly 8,950 feet. There are eight problems, running from V-easy up to V4-5. Four of them sit at V1, so there is plenty for newer boulderers, while the smaller uphill block carries the harder lines. Landings are flat and the stone is clean. You walk up from the Lake George access road, and the walk is short.

ca_way_warm_up_wall.blurb: Way Warm-up Wall is a compact vertical wall of eight boulder problems near T J Lake, above Mammoth Lakes in the Eastern Sierra, at about 9,300 feet. Most problems are easy: the grades begin at V-easy, three are V0, and the hardest two reach V4 and V5. Expect cracks, crimps and side pulls rather than big moves. The wall sits behind a stand of trees up and to the left of the neighbouring slabs, and the landings in this part of T J Slabs are decent, which makes it a good place to loosen up before harder problems nearby.

ca_snack_boulder.blurb: Snack Boulder is a large, squat block with a flat base among the boulders at the foot of The Old Woman in Hidden Valley Campground, Joshua Tree National Park. It has eight problems on monzogranite, and nearly all are very easy: seven are V-easy and one is V1. That makes it a good stop for beginners, children or anyone warming up, and the top is an easy downclimb. To find it, pass around the left end of School Boulder and follow a rough trail through rocks and brush.

ca_anasazi_wall.blurb: Anasazi Wall is a small wall on Petroglyph Rock in the Echo Rock area of central Joshua Tree National Park, close to Hidden Valley. It has eight climbs on monzogranite, mostly trad, with a single bolted sport route. Two climbs are easy at 5.5, and the other six are at the 5.10 level, so the wall splits between gentle outings and harder leads. The walk from the Echo Rock lot is cross-country and quick.

ca_victory_boulder.blurb: Victory Boulder is a small block beside the trail on the Real Hidden Valley loop in Joshua Tree National Park, near the Houser Buttress landmark. It has eight problems on good-quality granodiorite, nearly all of them gentle: five are V-easy, two are V0 and one is V2. That suits beginners and families. It takes about five minutes from the Real Hidden Valley lot, following the marked trail west along the foot of the rocky hillside. The loop it sits on draws large crowds on weekends, holidays and spring break.

_skipped.ca_seafarer_rock: No fetched page names Seafarer Rock or Ocean Cove; searches and the Sonoma Coast / Salt Point / Twin Coves pages turned up nothing for it, so not even one page about the crag itself.

_conflicts.ca_sister_boulder: Stored rock is rhyolite, but the Lake George boulder page (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/119398965/lake-george) describes the boulders there as granite; the crag's own page (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/119399030/sister-boulder) names no rock. No rock named in blurb.
